ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p463/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p463/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p463/r7.claim: The passage depicts cosmic upheaval and the collapse of social bonds; each person would offer even close family and tribe as ransom, while Hell burns and seizes those who evaded the call and hoarded wealth.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p463/r7.anchor: The flames of Hell shall tear and burn his skin

QASHANI:70:17-21/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:70:17-21/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:70:17-21/r1.claim: The denial of ransom rebukes escape: a person deserves punishment through the constitution of the self and is drawn to hell by affinity with it.
QASHANI:70:17-21/r1.anchor: فإنه بهيئة أجرامه استحق عذابه وبمناسبة نفسه للجحيم انجر إليها

QASHANI:70:17-21/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:70:17-21/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:70:17-21/r2.claim: Nature’s lower fire calls those turned from truth and holiness toward dark matter; natural affinity draws them into its spiritual flame, which seizes the heart, so escape is impossible.
QASHANI:70:17-21/r2.anchor: ما استدعت إلا المدبر عن الحق المعرض عن جناب القدس وعالم النور

QUSHAYRI:v3p351/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p351/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p351/r2.claim: Hell calls the unbeliever and hypocrite who turned away, summoning them toward itself.
QUSHAYRI:v3p351/r2.anchor: تقول جهنم للكافر والمنافق : يا فلان

QUSHAYRI:v3p351/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p351/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p351/r3.claim: As an inward sign, worldly life is a hell that hooks the heart with greed, drags it into accumulation, and makes people prefer wealth even to family; few escape its deception.
QUSHAYRI:v3p351/r3.anchor: والإشارة فيه : أن جهنم الدنيا تعلق بقلب المرء فتدعوه بكلاب الحرص إلى نفسه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p274/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p274/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p274/r3.claim: On the raised reading, one can understand the Fire truly calling people by their names and their fathers' names, with God creating speech in it as He does in body parts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p274/r3.anchor: أي حقيقة يخلق الله فيها الكلام كما يخلقه في الأعضاء، قاله ابن عباس وغيره، تدعوهم بأسمائهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p274/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p274/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p274/r4.claim: He compares the Fire's speaking to speech created in a tree; Abu Hayyan notes that this preserves the Mu'tazilite position.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p274/r4.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وكما خلقه في الشجرة. انتهى، فلم يترك مذهب الاعتزال.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p274/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p274/r5.speaker: الخليل وثعلب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p274/r5.claim: Al-Khalil reads تدعو figuratively as the Fire drawing near and inflicting torment; Tha'lab says it means destroy, an Arabic idiom also cited from al-Khalil and illustrated with poetry.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p274/r5.anchor: وقال ثعلب: يهلك، تقول العرب: دعا الله، أي أهلكك، وحكاه الخليل عن العرب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p274/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p274/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p274/r6.claim: Another reading assigns the calling to Hell's keepers but attributes it to the Fire; the summoned are those who turned away from truth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p274/r6.anchor: وقيل: تدعو، أي خزنة جهنم، أضيف دعاؤهم إليها، من أدبر عن الحق، وتولى

FARRA:v3p185/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p185/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p185/r1.claim: The call to those who turn away addresses each unbeliever or hypocrite individually by name.
FARRA:v3p185/r1.anchor: تقول للكافر: يا كافر إلي، يا منافق إلي، فتدعو كل واحد باسمه.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p223#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p223#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p223#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says Hell calls unbelievers and hypocrites by name in eloquent speech, then snatches them like a bird picking grain.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p223#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: تدعو الكافرين والمنافقين بأسمائهم بلسان فصيح ثم تلتقطهم كما يلتقط الطير الحب.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p223#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p223#2/r2.speaker: الخليل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p223#2/r2.claim: Al-Khalil interprets تدعو as ‘punishes,’ supported by the Arabic expression ‘May God call you,’ meaning ‘may God punish you.’
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p223#2/r2.anchor: حكي عن الخليل: أنه قال: تدعو أي تعذب. وقال: قال أعرابي لآخر: دعاك الله أي عذبك الله.

NAHHAS:v5p29/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p29/r17.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p29/r17.claim: Figuratively, Hell's keepers call those who turned from God's obedience; Qatada says it calls those who turned from the Book and its due rights too.
NAHHAS:v5p29/r17.anchor: مجاز لأنه يروى أن خزنتها ينادون إيتونا بمن أدبر وتولى عن طاعة الله

BIQAI-FULL:v8p149/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p149/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p149/r1.claim: The fire's calling may be metaphorical for drawing sinners to it or literal speech summoning a polytheist or hypocrite before it catches them like birds picking grain.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p149/r1.anchor: إلي يا مشرك إلي يا منافق

BIQAI-FULL:v8p149/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p149/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p149/r2.claim: It summons anyone who turned away from the truth or from deeds that could save them; turning away means deliberately making one's original sound nature reject the path of salvation.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p149/r2.anchor: من وقع منه إدبارهما من حقه الإقبال عليه سواء كان ذلك الإدبار عنها أو عن الأعمال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p367/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p367/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p367/r9.claim: Those who turned away and rejected faith are the ones summoned by the Fire.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p367/r9.anchor: وقوله تعالى: تدعوا من أدبر وتولى يريد الكفار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p367/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p367/r10.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p367/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas and others take the Fire's summons literally: it calls people by their own and their fathers' names.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p367/r10.anchor: واختلف الناس في دعائها، فقال ابن عباس وغيره: هو حقيقة تدعوهم بأسمائهم وأسماء آبائهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p367/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p367/r11.speaker: الخليل بن أحمد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p367/r11.claim: Al-Khalil reads the summons figuratively as the Fire's eagerness for them, drawing them near to its punishment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p367/r11.anchor: وقال الخليل بن أحمد هي عبارة عن حرصها عليهم واستدنائها لهم، وما توقعه من عذابها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p367/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p367/r12.speaker: ثعلب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p367/r12.claim: Thalab says تدعو means destroy, as in the Arab expression دعك الله, may God destroy you.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p367/r12.anchor: وقال ثعلب: تدعوا، معناه: تهلك، تقول العرب: دعاك الله أي أهلكك

ZAJJAJ:v5p221/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p221/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p221/r1.claim: Hell calls the disbeliever and hypocrite by name.

THALABI:v10p38/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p38/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p38/r10.claim: The Fire calls those who turned away from faith and truth, summoning them toward itself.
THALABI:v10p38/r10.anchor: تدعوا إلى نفسها من أدبر عن الإيمان وتولى عن الحق فتقول إلي إلي

THALABI:v10p38/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p38/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p38/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas says Hell calls disbelievers and hypocrites by name in a clear voice, then picks them up like a bird picking grain.
THALABI:v10p38/r12.anchor: قال ابن عباس: تدعوا الكافرين والمنافقين بأسمائهم بلسان فصيح، ثم تلتقطهم

THALABI:v10p38/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p38/r13.speaker: تغلب
THALABI:v10p38/r13.claim: Taghlib takes tadʿu to mean that Hell destroys; Arabs use the expression God called you to mean God destroyed you.
THALABI:v10p38/r13.anchor: وقال تغلب: تدعوا أي تهلك يقول العرف: دعاك الله أي أهلكك الله

THALABI:v10p38/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p38/r14.speaker: الخليل
THALABI:v10p38/r14.claim: Al-Khalil says the Fire's call is not an invitation to approach; it gives it power to punish those it calls.
THALABI:v10p38/r14.anchor: وقال الخليل: إنه ليس كالدعاء تعالوا ولكن دعوتها إياهم تمكنها من تعذيبهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r1.claim: Muqatil says the fire strips the scalp and limbs, burning away all flesh and skin.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل: تنزع النار الهامة (¬4) والأطراف، فلا تترك لحما ولا جلدا إلا أحرقته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r2.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r2.claim: Most exegetes and linguists, including Mujahid, identify الشوى as the limbs.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r2.anchor: وأكثر المفسرين (¬1) على أنها: الأطراف، (وهو قول مجاهد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r3.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr identifies الشوى as sinews and heels.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r3.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: للعصب والعقب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r4.claim: Abu Ishaq says الشوى means the flesh of the lower legs.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r5.speaker: ثابت البناني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r5.claim: Thabit al-Bunani says it means the finest features of human faces.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r5.anchor: وقال ثابت البناني: لمكارم وجه بني آدم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r6.speaker: الأعشى
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r6.claim: Al-Aʿsha's poetic use of شواته is cited as linguistic evidence for the term الشوى.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r6.anchor: ومنه قول الأعشى: قالت قتيلة ما له ... قدجللت شيبا شواته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says the fire calls those who turned away from Islam by identifying them as polytheists, unbelievers, hypocrites, wrongdoers, and sinners.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r7.anchor: ابن عباس: تدعو (¬8) من أدبر عن الإسلام، ودعاؤها أن تقول: إلي يا مشرك، إلي يا كافر، إلي يا منافق، إلي يا فاسق، إلي يا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r8.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r8.claim: Muqatil pictures the fire calling its own people to it; the exegetes say it calls those who turned from truth by name.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r8.anchor: وقال مقاتل: تدعو (1) النار يوم القيامة: إلي أهلي، إلي أهلي (2). فهذا دعاؤها، وهذا قول المفسرين؛ قالوا: تدعو

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r9.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r9.claim: Al-Mubarrad says تدعو means to torture, citing the idiom that God called someone by making him suffer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r9.anchor: تدعو من أدبر عن الحق باسمه (3). وقال المبرد: تدعو معناه بعذاب (4). روى عمرو عن أبيه: الداعي المعذب دعاه الله، أي: عذبه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p612/r25.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p612/r25.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p612/r25.claim: The Fire’s calling is figurative for bringing people into view, as though it calls and they appear.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p612/r25.anchor: { تدعوا } مجاز عن إحضارهم ، كأنها تدعوهم فتحضرهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p613/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p613/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p613/r1.claim: Poetic usages support the image of the Fire calling people forth; Dhū al-Rummah’s lines use tadʿū, and Abū al-Najm says the scout is told that pasture has grown and to descend.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p613/r1.anchor: تدعو أنفه الربب ; وقوله : ليالى اللهو يطبيني فأتبعه ; وقول أبي النجم : تقول للرائد أعشبت انزل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p613/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p613/r2.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p613/r2.claim: One view makes the Fire address people explicitly: “Come here, disbeliever, hypocrite.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p613/r2.anchor: وقيل : تقول لهم : إلي إلي يا كافر يا منافق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p613/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p613/r3.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p613/r3.claim: Another report says the Fire calls disbelievers and hypocrites in clear speech, then picks them up like grain; God may create speech in it as He does in human limbs and a tree.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p613/r3.anchor: تدعو المنافقين والكافرين بلسان فصيح ثم تلتقطهم التقاط الحب ، فيجوز أن يخلق الله فيها كلاما كما يخلقه في جلودهم وأيديهم وأرجلهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p613/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p613/r4.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p613/r4.claim: Alternatively, the calling is the summons of the Fire’s guardians.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p613/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p613/r5.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p613/r5.claim: A further interpretation takes tadʿū to mean “destroy,” from the Arabic expression daʿāka Allāh; the cited verse uses that idiom.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p613/r5.anchor: وقيل : تدعو تهلك ، من قول العرب : دعاك الله ، أي : أهلكك . قال : دعاك الله من رجل بأفعى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p613/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p613/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p613/r6.claim: The people summoned are those who turn away from the truth and then turn away from God’s command.

RAZI-FULL:v30p113#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p113#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p113#2/r1.claim: One view is a figurative call: the places in Hell destined for each disbeliever summon and bring them, as the earth may answer a question through reflection rather than a roar.
RAZI-FULL:v30p113#2/r1.anchor: كما قيل : سل الأرض من أشق أنهارك ، وغرس أشجارك

RAZI-FULL:v30p113#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p113#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p113#2/r2.claim: Another view says God creates speech in the Fire, which literally calls disbelievers and hypocrites before seizing them.
RAZI-FULL:v30p113#2/r2.anchor: حتى تقول صريحا : إلي يا كافر ، إلي يا منافق

RAZI-FULL:v30p113#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p113#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p113#2/r3.claim: A third view takes the Fire’s callers to be its keepers, with the keepers omitted from the wording.
RAZI-FULL:v30p113#2/r3.anchor: المراد أن زبانية النار يدعون فأضيف ذلك الدعاء إلى النار بحذف المضاف

RAZI-FULL:v30p113#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p113#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p113#2/r4.claim: A fourth view derives tadʿū from an Arabic usage meaning “destroy you,” as in the curse daʿāka Allāh.
RAZI-FULL:v30p113#2/r4.anchor: تدعو تهلك من قول العرب دعاك الله أي أهلكك

RAZI-FULL:v30p113#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p113#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p113#2/r5.claim: The phrase describes those who turn away from obedience and from faith.
RAZI-FULL:v30p113#2/r5.anchor: وقوله : { من أدبر وتولى } يعني من أدبر عن الطاعة وتولى عن الإيمان

RAZI-FULL:v30p113#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p113#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p113#2/r7.claim: Turning away marks rejection of knowing and obeying God; gathering marks greed and hoarding marks worldly attachment, the roots of religious affliction.
RAZI-FULL:v30p113#2/r7.anchor: فقوله : { أدبر وتولى } إشارة إلى الإعراض عن معرفة الله وطاعته ، وقوله : { وجمع فأوعى } إشارة إلى حب الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v30p113#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p113#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p113#2/r8.claim: Rāzī concludes that these two traits comprise the principal sources of religious corruption.
RAZI-FULL:v30p113#2/r8.anchor: ولا شك أن مجامع آفات الدين ليست إلا هذه

STUDYQURAN:70:17/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:70:17/r1.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:70:17/r1.claim: The Fire summons those destined for it because in worldly life they turned from obedience, belief in God’s books and messengers, or the truth.
STUDYQURAN:70:17/r1.anchor: The Fire will summon those who are destined for it, because during the life of this world they turned away from obedience to God and fled from belief in God’s books and God’s messengers or from the truth (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:70:17/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:70:17/r2.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:70:17/r2.claim: The Fire then picks out those who turned their backs on the truth in worldly life.
STUDYQURAN:70:17/r2.anchor: Then the Fire will pick out those who turned their backs and fled from the truth in the life of this world (IK)

TAB-FULL:v23p265/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p265/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p265/r1.claim: Qatāda glosses turning away as turning from God’s obedience, and turning aside as turning from His Book and its due.
TAB-FULL:v23p265/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {تدعو من أدبر وتولى} [المعارج: 17] قال: عن طاعة الله

TAB-FULL:v23p265/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p265/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p265/r2.claim: Mujāhid glosses the turning away as turning from the truth.
TAB-FULL:v23p265/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {تدعو من أدبر وتولى} [المعارج: 17] قال: عن الحق

TAB-FULL:v23p265/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p265/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v23p265/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says the Fire has power only over the disgraced unbeliever who turns from God, not over one who believes in God and His Messenger.
TAB-FULL:v23p265/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {تدعو من أدبر وتولى} [المعارج: 17] قال: ليس لها سلطان إلا على هوان من كفر وتولى

TABATABAI:70:11-18/r18.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:70:11-18/r18.speaker: author
TABATABAI:70:11-18/r18.claim: The Fire calls those who turned away from faith and worship, gathered wealth, hoarded it, and did not spend on the asker or deprived; this fits the following exception and mention of prayer and spending.
TABATABAI:70:11-18/r18.anchor: أي تطلب من أدبر عن الدعوة الإلهية إلى الإيمان بالله وأعرض عن عبادته تعالى وجمع المال

BURSEVI:v10p122#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p122#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p122#2/r4.claim: Those who turn away from truth and its recognition are drawn to the Fire and brought into it; calling them is a metaphor for bringing them present.
BURSEVI:v10p122#2/r4.anchor: أي عن الحق ومعرفته وهو مقابل أقبل ومعنى تدعو تجذب إلى نفسها وتحضر

BURSEVI:v10p122#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p122#2/r5.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v10p122#2/r5.claim: The Najmiyya interpretation takes turning back as failure to face God through obedience to the law and resistance to the lower nature.
BURSEVI:v10p122#2/r5.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية : من أدبر عن التوجه إلى الحق بموافقات الشريعة ومخالفات الطبيعة

BURSEVI:v10p122#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p122#2/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v10p122#2/r6.claim: It reads turning away as abandoning the approach to the afterlife and the turning away from worldly life.
BURSEVI:v10p122#2/r6.anchor: وتولى عن الإقبال على الآخرة والإدبار عن الدنيا

BURSEVI:v10p122#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p122#2/r7.speaker: القاشاني
BURSEVI:v10p122#2/r7.claim: Al-Qashani says like inclines to like: the Fire of lower nature summons those who turn from truth and the holy realm, face darkness, and love transient lower things, drawing them by natural affinity.
BURSEVI:v10p122#2/r7.anchor: وقال القاشاني : بمناسبة نفسه للجحيم أنجر إليها إذ الجنس إلى الجنس يميل

BURSEVI:v10p122#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p122#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p122#2/r8.claim: The Fire may call sinners aloud by their names and seize them like a bird picking up grain.
BURSEVI:v10p122#2/r8.anchor: أو تدعو الكافرين والمنافقين بلفظ فصيح بأسمائهم ثم تلقتطهم كالتقاط الطير الحبر

BURSEVI:v10p122#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p122#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p122#2/r9.claim: Alternatively, God creates speech in the Fire as He does in human skin and limbs or in a tree, enabling it to call the sinners.
BURSEVI:v10p122#2/r9.anchor: ويجوز يخلق الله فيها كلاما كما يخلقه في جلودهم وأيديهم وأرجلهم وكما خلقه في الشجرة

BURSEVI:v10p122#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p122#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p122#2/r10.claim: Alternatively, the Fire calls its keepers with an omitted possessive, or the verb is figuratively attributed to the Fire as the destination called toward.
BURSEVI:v10p122#2/r10.anchor: أو تدعو زبانيتها على حذف المضاف أو على الإسناد المجازي حيث أسند فعل الداعي إلى المدعو إليه

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r6.claim: The principal causes of entering hell are turning away from the Prophet's true religion and monotheism, and refusing to use one's wealth to help the needy or ease hardship.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r6.anchor: Peygamberin getirdiği hak dine, tevhid inancına sırt çevirmek, b) Servetinden muhtaçları faydalandırmamak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r7.claim: The Qur'an, especially its Meccan surahs, repeatedly criticizes both rejection of monotheism and selfish refusal to relieve people's material hardship.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r7.anchor: Kur’an-ı Kerîm’in bütününde, özellikle de Mekke’de inen sûrelerde onların en fazla eleştirilen kötülükleri olmuştur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r8.claim: The Qur'an's most comprehensive duties are recognizing God's existence and oneness and helping people with kindness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r8.anchor: Kur’an-ı Kerîm’in insanlığa yüklediği görevlerin en önemlisi ve en kuşatıcı olanı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r9.speaker: İslâm âlimleri
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r9.claim: Muslim scholars summarize these two duties as reverence for God's command and compassion for God's creatures.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r9.anchor: İslâm âlimleri bu iki büyük görevi kısaca “Allah’ın buyruğuna saygı, Allah’ın yarattıklarına şefkat” şeklinde özetlemişlerdir

BURHAN:v1p364/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p364/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p364/r4.claim: A permissible incomplete pause may have the same surface form as continuous recitation, as at the end of wa-tawallā in the description of the Fire.
BURHAN:v1p364/r4.anchor: ومنها أن تكون صورته فى اللفظ صورة الوصل بعينها نحو قوله تعالى ﴿ كلا إنها لظى نزاعة للشوى

BURHAN:v1p75/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p75/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p75/r6.claim: The sequence ending with “it calls whoever turned away and turned back” is another example of these fawāṣil.
BURHAN:v1p75/r6.anchor: كلا إنها لظى نزاعة للشوى تدعو من أدبر وتولى وجمع فأوعى

BURHAN:v1p75/r12.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p75/r12.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p75/r12.claim: Some rhetoricians instead name tarṣīʿ, where paired clauses use different words corresponding in meter, rhyme, and parallel arrangement; he says this ornate type does not occur in the Qur'an.
BURHAN:v1p75/r12.anchor: ومنهم من يذكر بدله الترصيع وهو أن يكون المتقدم من الفقرتين مؤلفا من كلمات مختلفة والثانى مؤلفا من مثلها فى ثلاثة أشياء

DAMGHANI:v1p173/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p173/r6.speaker: المبرد
DAMGHANI:v1p173/r6.claim: Al-Mubarrad glosses the Fire’s calling of those who turned away as tormenting them.
DAMGHANI:v1p173/r6.anchor: السابع : الدعاء العذاب ( والموت ) قوله تعالى في سورة المعارج

DAMGHANI:v1p173/r7.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p173/r7.speaker: ثعلب
DAMGHANI:v1p173/r7.claim: Thaʿlab says the idiom “May God call you” means “May God cause you to die.”
DAMGHANI:v1p173/r7.anchor: وقال ثعلب " دعاك الله أي أماتك الله

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r1.claim: Speech is figuratively attributed to something unable to speak: its condition is described as what it would say if it could speak.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r1.anchor: وإنما هذا عبارة: لكوناهما فكانتا. قال الشاعر حكاية عن ناقته

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r2.claim: A poet imagines a weary, exhausted she-camel complaining about her hardship, though she said nothing; the description infers what she would say if able.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r2.anchor: وهي لم تقل شيئا من هذا، ولكنه رآها في حال من الجهد والكلال

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r3.claim: Another poet says his camel complained of the long journey, a figurative report of how much travel he imposed on it.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r3.anchor: وكقول الآخر : شكا إلي جملي طول السرى

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r4.speaker: عنترة
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r4.claim: Antarah says his horse complained with a tear and whinny after a spear struck it; the horse is not literally complaining or shedding tears.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r4.anchor: وكقول عنترة في فرسه : فازور من وقع القنا بلبانه

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r6.claim: Hell calls those who turn away because they are destined to end up there; it is as if the destination itself summons them.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r6.anchor: يريد: أن مصير من أدبر وتولى إليها، فكأنها الداعية لهم

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r7.speaker: ذو الرمة
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r7.claim: Dhu al-Rumma's دعت ميّة الأعداد makes water sources seem to call Mayya when she leaves one water source for another.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r7.anchor: كما قال ذو الرمة : دعت مية الأعداد واستبدلت بها

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r8.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r8.claim: An anonymous poet says a valley calls its visitors; the fly's buzzing indicates nearby plants and water, as though it summoned them.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r8.anchor: وكقول الآخر : ولقد هبطت الواديين وواديا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r9.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r9.speaker: أبو النجم
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r9.claim: Abu al-Najm's flies seem to tell a herdsman that the pasture is green and he should descend, though their buzzing merely signals grass.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r9.anchor: وقال أبو النجم يذكر نبتا : مستأسدا ذبانه في غيطل

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r10.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r10.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r10.claim: An unnamed poet describes a wolf as asking the wind when it hears no sound, another figurative attribution of speech or inquiry.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p71/r10.anchor: وقال آخر يصف ذئبا : يستخبر الريح إذا لم يسمع

MAJAZ:v2p269/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p269/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p269/r4.claim: For humans, shawāt are the hands, feet, and head; al-Aʿshā’s word shawātahu is corrected by Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ to sarātahu.
MAJAZ:v2p269/r4.anchor: واحدتها شواة وهى اليدان والرجلان والرأس من الآدميين

MAJAZ:v2p269/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p269/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p269/r5.claim: He reports hearing a man in Medina say iqshaʿarrat shawātī, my limbs bristled, as evidence for the human use of shawā.
MAJAZ:v2p269/r5.anchor: وسمعت رجلا من أهل المدينة يقول اقشعرت شواتى

MAJAZ:v2p269/r6.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p269/r6.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p269/r6.claim: For a horse, shawā means its legs, as in ʿablu al-shawā; it is not used for the head, since horses are praised for slender cheeks and a refined face.
MAJAZ:v2p269/r6.anchor: ولا يكون هذا للرأس لأنهم وصفوا الخيل بأسالة الخدين وعتق الوجه ورقته

SAMIN-DURR:70:15#2/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:70:15#2/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:70:15#2/r10.claim: تدعو can be a predicate of إن, the predicate of an omitted subject, or circumstantial modifying لظى or نزاعة under either reading.

ASAD-NOTES:70:15/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:70:15/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:70:15/r3.claim: The flame claims those who turn away from what is right and truth, hoard wealth, and withhold it from others.
ASAD-NOTES:70:15/r3.anchor: It will claim all such as turn their backs

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p157/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p157/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p157/r4.claim: Hell calls those who turned from obedience and truth, while the constant worshippers turn toward obedience and are thereby saved from its punishment.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p157/r4.anchor: فإن ذلك الذي تدعوه جهنم، قد أدبر عن الطاعة وتولى عن الحق، وهذا مقبل على الطاعة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p157/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p157/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p157/r5.claim: The paired wording أدبر وتولى reinforces turning away, then answers it with إلا المصلين and the worshippers who remain constant in prayer.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p157/r5.anchor: وقال: (وتولى) وهو توكيد للإدبار والانصراف عن الطاعة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p159/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p159/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p159/r2.claim: The people who set aside a defined share for the asker and deprived are the opposite of those summoned by Hell for turning away and hoarding wealth.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p159/r2.anchor: فقد جعلوا في أموالهم حقا معلوما للسائل والمحروم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p160/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p160/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p160/r1.claim: One meaning of الشوى is human skin; Hell strips the skin and leaves the entrails exposed.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p160/r1.anchor: ومن معاني (الشوى) جلد الإنسان فهي، أي: جهنم تنزعُ جلدَ الإنسان

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p160/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p160/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p160/r2.claim: Skin protects the entrails as a container protects wealth; the hoarder who enclosed his money has his body's enclosing skin torn away and its contents exposed.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p160/r2.anchor: والجلد للأحشاء كالوعاء للمال يحفظ ما في داخله

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p160/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p160/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p160/r3.claim: The saying انج بجلدك marks skin as more precious to a person than wealth, making the punishment a fitting recompense of the same kind as the hoarding sin.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p160/r3.anchor: فانظر التناسق الجميل بين المعصية والعذاب، والجزاء من جنس العمل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p197/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p197/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p197/r3.claim: The greater punishment scene belongs in al-Maʿarij, which opens with punishment; thus the surah beginning with punishment contains punishment, and the one beginning with turning away contains flight.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p197/r3.anchor: فوضع مشهد العذاب في السورة التي تبدأ بالعذاب

ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r1.claim: On the nominative reading, tadʿū may be the predicate of an omitted subject, a nested or coordinate circumstantial clause, or a second predicate.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r1.anchor: خبر مبتدأ مقدر أو حال متداخلة أو مترادفة أو مفردة أو خبر بعد خبر على قراءة الرفع

ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r2.claim: One report says God gives the Fire speech, as He gives speech to skins and limbs, so it calls people by their names and their fathers’ names.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r2.anchor: وذلك كما روي عن ابن عباس وغيره يخلق الله تعالى فيها القدرة على الكلام كما يخلقه في جلودهم وأيديهم وأرجلهم فتناديهم بأسمائهم وأسماء آبائهم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r3.claim: Another report has the Fire calling, “Come to me, O unbeliever; come to me, O hypocrite.”
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r3.anchor: وروي أنها تقول لهم إلي إلي يا كافر يا منافق

ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r4.claim: The verb may mean attracting and bringing them in; Dhū al-Rumma’s verse about a bull’s nose being called by a cloud illustrates this use.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r4.anchor: وجوز أن يراد به الجذب والإحضار كما في قول ذي الرمة يصف الثور الوحشي

ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r5.speaker: ذو الرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r5.claim: A second line by Dhū al-Rumma, “the nights of pleasure entice me, so I follow,” supplies a parallel for drawing someone along.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r5.anchor: ليالي اللهو يطبيني فأتبعه كأنني ضارب في غمرة لعب

ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r6.claim: The Fire’s fitness or entitlement to receive them may be figuratively expressed as if it called them.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r6.anchor: ولا يبعد أن يقال شبه لياقتها لهم أو استحقاقهم لها على ما قيل بدعائها لهم فعبر عن ذلك بالدعاء على سبيل الاستعارة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r7.speaker: ثعلب والخليل
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r7.claim: Thaʿlab, with al-Khalīl reporting Arab usage, says tadʿū can mean “destroy”; lexicons also gloss calling harm down on someone and the calamities of time. Al-Ālūsī regards this as possible but uncommon and uncertain.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r7.anchor: وقال ثعلب تدعو تهلك من قول العرب دعاك الله تعالى أي أهلكك وحكاه الخليل عنهم وفي الأساس دعاه الله تعالى بما يكره أنزله به

ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r8.claim: A cited verse, “May God call down a serpent on you,” supports the unusual destructive sense of tadʿū.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r8.anchor: دعاك الله من رجل بأفعى إذا ناما العيون سرت عليكا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r9.claim: The call may be made by Hell’s keepers but figuratively attributed to the Fire, or an omitted “keepers” may be understood.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61/r9.anchor: وجوز أن يكون الدعاء لزبانيتها وأسند إليها مجازا أو الكلام على تقدير مضاف أي تدعو زبانيتها

ALUSI-FULL:v29p61#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61#2/r1.claim: Those who turned away from truth in worldly life are meant.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p61#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61#2/r2.claim: Tawallā means that they turned away from obedience.

BAYDAWI-FULL:70:13-17/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:70:13-17/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:70:13-17/r10.claim: The Fire draws in and brings near those who flee from it, metaphorically described as calling them.

BAYDAWI-FULL:70:13-17/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:70:13-17/r11.speaker: ذي الرمة
BAYDAWI-FULL:70:13-17/r11.claim: Dhu al-Rummah's verse uses tadʿū for drawing something toward oneself, supporting this sense.
BAYDAWI-FULL:70:13-17/r11.anchor:
كقول ذي الرمة:
تدعو أنفه الريب

BAYDAWI-FULL:70:13-17/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:70:13-17/r12.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:70:13-17/r12.claim: Alternatively, the Fire calls its keepers.

BAYDAWI-FULL:70:13-17/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:70:13-17/r13.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:70:13-17/r13.claim: Alternatively, “calls” means destroys, as in the idiom “God called him” meaning that God destroyed him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:70:13-17/r13.anchor: وقيل تدعو تهلك من قولهم دعاه الله إذا أهلكه

BAYDAWI-FULL:70:13-17/r14.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:70:13-17/r14.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:70:13-17/r14.claim: The ones who turn away have turned from truth and obedience.

DURR-FULL:v8p281/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p281/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p281/r6.claim: Mujahid says the person summoned is one who turned away from the truth.
DURR-FULL:v8p281/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله: {وفصيلته} قال: قبيلته وفي قوله: {نزاعة للشوى} قال: لجلود الرأس {تدعو من أدبر وتولى} قال: عن الحق

DURR-FULL:v8p281/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p281/r10.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p281/r10.claim: Qatada says adbara means turning away from obedience to God.
DURR-FULL:v8p281/r10.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه {نزاعة للشوى} قال: لهامته ومكارم وجهه {تدعو من أدبر} قال: عن طاعة الله تعالى

DURR-FULL:v8p281/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p281/r11.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p281/r11.claim: Qatada says tawallā means turning from God’s Book and its due right.
DURR-FULL:v8p281/r11.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه {نزاعة للشوى} قال: لهامته ومكارم وجهه {تدعو من أدبر} قال: عن طاعة الله تعالى {وتولى} قال: عن كتاب الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p162/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p162/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p162/r12.claim: The next verse makes the implied threat explicit: the Fire calls the one who rejected the call to monotheism, turned away, and cared only for hoarded wealth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p162/r12.anchor: وقد صرح بما وقع التعريض به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r1.claim: “It calls” is a second predicate with the nominative reading of “nazzāʿatan,” or a circumstantial clause under either reading.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r1.anchor: إما خبر ثان حسب قراءة { نزاعة } بالرفع وإما حال على القراءتين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r2.claim: One nonliteral reading makes the Fire a host summoning guests to a banquet, a sarcastic personification cued by the description of its victims.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r2.anchor: شبهت لظى في انهيال الناس إليها بضائف لمأدبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r3.claim: On that reading, tadʿū derives from the noun for an invitation, with the following description serving as a cue or elaboration.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r3.anchor: أي من أدبر وتولى عن الإيمان بالله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r4.claim: Another figurative reading portrays the unbelievers’ gathering at the Fire as its invitation to attend, using a dependent comparison to a caller’s summons.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r4.anchor: أو أن يشبه إحضار الكفار عندها بدعوتها إياهم للحضور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r5.speaker: ذو الرمة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r5.claim: Dhu al-Rummah’s line about a wild bull says that al-rabab plants “call” to its nose, cited for this figurative use of calling.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r5.anchor: كقول ذي الرمة يصف الثور الوحشي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r6.claim: A literal reading takes the callers to be Hell’s angels, with the attribution to Hell by place or cause.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r6.anchor: و ( الذين يدعون ) : هم الملائكة الموكلون بجهنم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r7.claim: Alternatively, Hell itself calls literally when God creates voices in it summoning the rejecters, then devours them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r7.anchor: بأن يخلق الله فيها أصواتا تنادي الذين تولوا أن يردوا عليها فتلتهمهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r8.claim: The description denotes the criminals who wish to ransom themselves from the punishment in 70:14.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r8.anchor: جنس الموصوفين بأنهم أدبروا وتولوا وجمعوا وهم المجرمون الذين يودون أن يفتدوا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r9.claim: These are traits of polytheists and consequences of shirk: rejecting and turning away from Islam, and hoarding wealth out of fear for it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p164/r9.anchor: وهذه الصفات خصائص المشركين ، وهي من آثار دين الشرك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p165/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p165/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p165/r1.claim: Adbara suggests turning one’s back from the outset; tawallā suggests leaving after having engaged, so the conjunction preserves a distinction rather than mere repetition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p165/r1.anchor: ففي التولي معنى إيثار غير المتولى عنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p165/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p165/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p165/r2.claim: Adbara depicts rejecting the Qur’an without listening from the beginning (41:26); tawallā depicts turning away after hearing it (8:31). Both states characterize the polytheists and warrant punishment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p165/r2.anchor: والتولي مستعار للإعراض عن القرآن بعد سماعه وللنفور عن دعوة الرسول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p165/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p165/r3.speaker: الكشاف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p165/r3.claim: Al-Kashshāf assigns both verbs the same object: turning away from the truth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p165/r3.anchor: وفي ( الكشاف ) : أدبر عن الحق وتولى عنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p165/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p165/r4.speaker: البيضاوي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p165/r4.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī assigns separate objects: he rejects truth, meaning faith, and turns from obedience after hearing the Messenger’s call.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p165/r4.anchor: فقدر البيضاوي : أدبر عن الحق وتولى عن الطاعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p165/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p165/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p165/r5.claim: Qatādah reverses the objects: turning away from God’s obedience and from God’s Book; al-Fakhr and al-Nīsābūrī follow this view.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p165/r5.anchor: وعن قتادة عكسه : أدبر عن طاعة الله وتولى عن كتاب الله وتبعه الفخر والنيسابوري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p362/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p362/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p362/r1.claim: It calls those who turned away from faith and turned away from the truth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p362/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى تدعو من أدبر عن الإيمان وتولى عن الحق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p362/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p362/r2.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p362/r2.claim: The Fire calls, “Come here, polytheist; come here, hypocrite.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p362/r2.anchor: قال المفسرون تقول إلي يا مشرك إلي يا منافق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p225#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p225#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p225#2/r1.claim: The Fire summons those destined for it, people created for the Fire who were fated to do its deeds in worldly life.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p225#2/r1.anchor: أبناءها الذين خلقهم الله لها، وقدر لهم أنهم في الدار الدنيا يعملون عملها،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p225#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p225#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p225#2/r2.claim: On the Resurrection Day the Fire calls clearly and fluently, then snatches its people from the gathering as a bird picks up grain.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p225#2/r2.anchor: فتدعوهم يوم القيامة بلسان طلق ذلق، ثم تلتقطهم من بين أهل المحشر كما يلتقط الطير الحب.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p225#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p225#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p225#2/r3.claim: Turning away means denying with the heart and abandoning deeds with the limbs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p225#2/r3.anchor: أي: كذب بقلبه، وترك العمل بجوارحه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r6.speaker: الفراء
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r6.claim: Al-Farra says Hell calls people by name, summoning an unbeliever or hypocrite to itself.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r6.anchor: أحدها : أنها تدعوهم بأسمائهم فتقول للكافر : يا كافر إلي , وللمنافق : يا منافق إلي , قاله الفراء .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r7.claim: Alternatively, their destination is Hell, so it is as though it calls them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r7.anchor: الثاني : أن مصير من أدبر وتولى إليها , فكأنها الداعية لهم , ومثله قول الشاعر :

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r8.claim: The poet's mute buzzing fly illustrates figurative calling: its buzzing alerts people to it without literal speech.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r8.anchor: ولقد هبطنا الواديين فواديا يدعو الأنيس به العضيض الأبكم

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r9.claim: A third view makes the callers the keepers of Hell, whose call is attributed to the Fire.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r9.anchor: الثالث : الداعي خزنة جهنم أضيف دعاؤهم إليها , لأنهم يدعون إليها .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r10.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r10.claim: Mujahid says the person turned away from obedience and turned from the truth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r10.anchor: أحدها : أدبر عن الطاعة وتولى عن الحق , قاله مجاهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r11.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r11.claim: Muqatil says he turned away from faith and turned toward unbelief.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r11.anchor: الثاني : أدبر عن الإيمان وتولى إلى الكفر , قاله مقاتل .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r12.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r12.claim: Qatada says he turned away from God's command and turned from His Book.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r12.anchor: الثالث : أدبر عن أمر الله وتولى عن كتاب الله , قاله قتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r13.claim: Another explanation is that he turned away from acceptance and turned away from action.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r13.anchor: الرابع : أدبر عن القبول وتولى عن العمل .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r14.claim: The person who turned away gathered wealth and stored it in a container, withholding God's due.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r14.anchor: يعني الذي أدبر وتولى جمع المال فأوعى , بأن جعله في وعاء حفظا له ومنعا لحق الله منه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r15.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p93/r15.claim: Qatada characterizes him as relentlessly accumulating and withholding wealth.

MUQATIL:70:8-18/r12.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:70:8-18/r12.speaker: author
MUQATIL:70:8-18/r12.claim: On Judgment Day the Fire calls those who turned their backs on faith and turned toward unbelief.
MUQATIL:70:8-18/r12.anchor: تدعو النار يوم القيامة، تقول: إلى أهلى فهذا دعاؤها لمن أدبر عن الإيمان { وتولى } [آية: 17]

NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#8/r1.claim: The Fire calls sinners by name, destroys them, or their destination is described as calling them.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#8/r1.anchor: من قولهم دعاك الله أي اهلكلك أو لما كان مصيره اليها جعلت كانها دعته

NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#8/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#8/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#8/r2.claim: Those called are people who turned away from the truth and obedience.

QURTUBI-FULL:70:16-17/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:16-17/r19.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:70:16-17/r19.claim: Laza calls those who turned away from God's obedience and faith in worldly life, summoning them as disbelievers and polytheists.
QURTUBI-FULL:70:16-17/r19.anchor: أي تدعو لظى من أدبر في الدنيا عن طاعة الله وتولى عن الإيمان.

QURTUBI-FULL:70:16-17/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:16-17/r20.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:70:16-17/r20.claim: Ibn Abbas says it calls disbelievers and hypocrites by name in a clear voice, then snatches them as a bird picks up grain.
QURTUBI-FULL:70:16-17/r20.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: تدعو الكافرين والمنافقين بأسمائهم بلسان فصيح

QURTUBI-FULL:70:16-17/r21.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:16-17/r21.speaker: ثعلب
QURTUBI-FULL:70:16-17/r21.claim: Thaʿlab interprets tadʿū as destroy, citing the Arab expression daʿāka Allāh for may God destroy you.
QURTUBI-FULL:70:16-17/r21.anchor: وقال ثعلب: «تدعو» أي تهلك. تقول العرب: دعاك الله أي أهلكك الله.

QURTUBI-FULL:70:16-17/r22.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:16-17/r22.speaker: الخليل
QURTUBI-FULL:70:16-17/r22.claim: Al-Khalil says the call is not an invitation to come, but its power to summon them into torment.
QURTUBI-FULL:70:16-17/r22.anchor: وقال الخليل: إنه ليس كالدعاء «تعالوا» ولكن دعوتها إياهم تمكنها من تعذيبهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:70:16-17/r23.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:16-17/r23.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:70:16-17/r23.claim: Another view says the keepers of Hell are the callers, with their call attributed to Hell.
QURTUBI-FULL:70:16-17/r23.anchor: وقيل: الداعي خزنة جهنم أضيف دعاؤهم إليها.

QURTUBI-FULL:70:16-17/r24.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:16-17/r24.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:70:16-17/r24.claim: Another view takes the wording as a figure: the fate of those who turned away is Hell, so it is as though Hell called them.
QURTUBI-FULL:70:16-17/r24.anchor: وقيل هو ضرب مثل أي إن مصير من أدبر
